decisionMemo.businessProblem: A B2B payments SaaS growing 50% has a deteriorating expansion engine: NRR fell from 110% to 100% and expansion bookings collapsed from 38% to 19% of bookings, while gross retention (94%), new-logo win rate (~31%), and product satisfaction (NPS 44) all held steady. The owner reads this as price pressure from larger discounting entrants and wants to cut take-rates across the board. But the cross-sell modules that should drive expansion are barely sold: payouts attached to 22% of the base, virtual cards 9%, FX 6%, with only ~30% of AP customers ever pitched a second module, and the company has zero expansion-quota or account-management capacity. Competitive take-rate losses are confined to the top 10% highest-volume prospects, not the broad base. With NRR gating the Series B raise and 26 months of runway, the owner must choose within 30 days between a margin-eroding blanket price cut and rebuilding a structured expansion motion.
